title: MEMO_TEXT whose bytes are not valid UTF-8
description: A text memo holding the single byte 0xff. XDR string<28> is a byte string and stellar-core does not require UTF-8, so a reader that decodes the memo into a native string and writes it back changes the bytes, and with them the transaction hash.

shapes.note: Length is bounded by XDR (28 bytes); content is passed through. To be confirmed against core source for the guide.

provenance.method: Written by hand: discriminant 1 (MEMO_TEXT), length 1, byte 0xff, three padding bytes.
provenance.rationale: Hand-built because it is a bare Memo. js-stellar-sdk#1823 states that such bytes are valid on the network, and the RFP lists memos among the fields core passes through. A ledger entry with a transaction carrying this memo is planned as a local-core companion.

decoded.why: SEP-51 escapes the byte; it is not replaced by U+FFFD.

operations.why: Reading the memo as a native string and building a new memo from it must give the same bytes or fail. 0000000100000003efbfbd00 is the wrong answer.

notes: Bytes are the example from the issue. Both verdicts were measured on 2026-11-17 with the published npm packages (repro/README.md): reading the memo through the .value getter and rebuilding gives 0000000100000003efbfbd00 on v17.2.1 and on v17.3.0. The upstream fix (#1824) documents the getter as lossy and keeps the behaviour, so the post-fix verdict is still 'diverged': the entry records a documented hazard, not a regression.
